purpose: Stable decision-relevant benchmark questions for solver-research queryability. Required cases must remain mechanically answerable; known-gap cases document missing source structure or query capability without pretending they are solved.

benchmarks.question: What question support depends on the WS1 retained-evidence result report?
Which current workstream gates can advance without fresh solver/reference execution?
Which evidence reports have successor questions that are still live?
Which terminal questions still constrain live questions?
Which measurement opportunities are shared by multiple questions?
Which research blocks have been consumed by multiple questions?
Where do stable ownership/provenance links still fall back to lexical discovery or no owner?
Is the graph internally connected without unresolved authored references, and are current workstream gates structurally classified?
What became newly answerable after a specific asset, observer, capability, or commit was added?
Which research-system audits or architecture findings still have live successors or unpropagated lessons?
benchmarks.gap: Current research-system findings now have stable derived IDs and snapshots, and structured questionless reports expose report-level successors; individual architecture findings still do not author resolvedBy/successor links.

benchmarks.question: Which conclusions would actually become unsupported if one evidence source were withdrawn, accounting for redundant support?
benchmarks.gap: Explicit decisionSupport semantics now distinguish necessity/redundancy where authored. Most historical questions still expose answeredBy evidence trails without sufficiency semantics, so support-withdrawal consequences remain unknown there.

benchmarks.question: Can current research-system architecture/lifecycle findings be addressed by stable machine identity and diffed over time?
